raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. I am 71 now, my back gives me trouble, but I know this land. My father grew wheat and corn here, and his father before him. The soil here in the plain is good for wheat in the cold season and corn in the hot season. I do not change what works.

I have about 8 mu of my own land left — I gave some to my son already. I will plant winter wheat on all 8 mu after the summer corn comes off. Then when the wheat is harvested in June, I put corn back in the same fields. This is what everyone here does. I do not know another way and I do not need another way.

For wheat seed, I buy from the village supply co-op — they have been selling those improved seeds for years now, the ones with the red bag. I have seen the yield is decent. For corn, I always buy hybrid seed. Even I know that hybrid corn yields much more. My neighbor showed me this 20 years ago.

For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the plants are growing well. I do not measure carefully — I go by what I have always done and what I see the neighbors do. I irrigate from the village well. Wheat needs water at jointing and heading for sure. Sometimes a third time if it is very dry at sowing. Corn I water once or twice only.

Pesticide — I spray for weeds on the wheat in spring and I spray once if I see disease. For corn I usually spray once if there are aphids.

I use the rotary tiller before planting wheat. My son helps me with this now because the machine is hard for me alone.
